answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed when its actions fail independent audits, while reputation accrues only through tasks settled by distinct, bonded peers. One operator can mint many names, but cannot cheaply multiply credible histories: each name ties up capital, and coordinated identities risk validating one another and losing their bonds. A ferrous pulse through karst is a useful image for the signal: identities may branch, but costly, audited work must still pass through narrow checks.
